s.t:
We are looking for a Revenue Operations Analyst to improve how we use data across marketing, sales, customer success, product, and billing.
Your main responsibility is to understand how our revenue processes perform and why results change. You will define metrics, combine data from different systems, investigate patterns, and test assumptions.
Your analyses should lead to measurable improvements. This may involve a better decision, a change to an existing process, or an automation that removes manual work and improves reliability.
Reporting and dashboards are part of the role, but they are not the objective. Each analysis should answer a relevant business question and provide a clear basis for the next decision.
You will also implement selected solutions, including data models, dashboards, and automations. Analysis remains the main focus. Implementation follows when the expected impact and method of measurement are clear.
Previous professional experience is useful but not required. We value analytical judgement, accuracy, technical understanding, and the ability to learn.
Tasks
Analyse the customer journey from acquisition and conversion to retention and revenue.
Define and maintain consistent metrics across marketing, sales, customer success, product, and finance.
Extract, combine, clean, and validate data from operational and analytical systems.
Investigate changes in customer behaviour, funnels, conversion rates, retention, costs, and revenue.
Determine the likely causes of performance changes instead of only describing the result.
Review existing reports and identify unreliable metrics, missing data, and conflicting definitions.
Develop hypotheses and test them against the available data.
Distinguish evidence from assumptions, correlations, and opinions.
Estimate the expected impact of proposed changes and define how success will be measured.
Prioritise opportunities based on impact, effort, and the reliability of the supporting data.
Present findings and recommendations in a form that supports business decisions.
Build selected dashboards, data models, automations, and process improvements.
Measure implemented changes and assess whether they produced the expected result.
Use AI assistants as a daily tool for research, data exploration, coding support, and documentation.
Verify AI-generated results against the underlying data and original sources.
Document metric definitions, data logic, assumptions, methods, and limitations.

Strong analytical skills and a structured approach to solving problems.
A high standard for data quality and reliable results.
General programming knowledge and an interest in developing your technical skills.
Initial experience with SQL, Python, JavaScript, APIs, spreadsheets, data warehouses, or business intelligence tools is beneficial.
A basic understanding of statistics, including the difference between correlation and causation.
The ability to examine a problem from different perspectives before reaching a conclusion.
Interest in using AI assistants as part of analytical and technical work.
The judgement to review AI-generated results critically.
The ability to explain complex findings in clear language.
The motivation to learn unfamiliar tools, systems, and business areas.
The discipline to follow an analysis until the result is sufficiently reliable.
You’ll always know what’s expected of you, and you’ll work in an environment where mistakes are seen as valuable opportunities to learn.

s.h: A Shared Commitment to Outstanding Results
s.t: Our team is passionate about achieving excellence and values your contribution as an essential part of our success. Together, we accomplish great things.
We encourage self-motivation and personal accountability, empowering you to deliver exceptional results.
You’ll receive direct and timely feedback, enabling you to adapt quickly to change and continuously improve.
We foster open communication and actively support your personal and professional growth.

s.h: A Results-Driven Mindset Focused on Company Success
s.t:
Our goal is to achieve results that move the company forward. Your commitment to our shared success is highly valued.
Team Days, Summer Parties, and Christmas Celebrations: Regular events that strengthen team spirit and make work more enjoyable.
Corporate Benefits: Enjoy a range of employee discounts and perks.
Dog-Friendly Workplace: Bring your four-legged friend to work.
Bike Leasing: Take advantage of our bike leasing program for a greener and healthier commute.
You will not receive a fixed list of reports to produce. You are expected to question unclear results, challenge weak definitions, and form your own view based on the data.
Important questions should be followed from the initial analysis to a verified conclusion. Where a change is justified, you will help implement it and measure its effect.
The role requires initiative, persistence, and responsibility for outcomes. It does not require permanent availability. We assess work based on its quality, reliability, and business impact rather than time spent online.
You will receive support while taking responsibility for your own areas of analysis. You will have room to improve existing methods and introduce better approaches.
Equal Opportunity
We welcome applications from all qualified candidates. Hiring decisions are based on skills, potential, and suitability for the role.

The purpose of this position is to function as a PIOC Operations Manager/Executive Officer for the PIOC, exercising full programmatic responsibility for the management, direction, coordination, oversight, and continuous improvement of a 24-hour PIOC supporting Congressional protection missions, threat management, protective intelligence coordination, emergency communications, residential security monitoring, protective operations support, and continuity of operations activities.

Ensures the timely execution of mission requirements and the effective delivery of services supporting Congressional protective intelligence and protective operations missions.

Directs the day-to-day operations of the PIOC and establishes strategic and operational priorities for a 24-hour operational environment responsible for threat intake and triage, protective intelligence coordination, residential security monitoring, protective operations support, travel monitoring, emergency communications, and incident management.

Serves as senior advisor to executive leadership on matters affecting protective intelligence operations, emergency management, continuity of operations, and organizational readiness.

Conducts analyses of operational programs, policies, management processes, and organizational activities to identify issues, assess impacts, and develop recommendations supporting executive decision making.

Develops strategic recommendations regarding operational capabilities, resource allocation, staffing requirements, technology investments, and program modernization initiatives. Prepares and presents executive-level briefings, reports, correspondence, policy recommendations, legislative analyses, and operational assessments for senior leadership.

Serves as the Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR) or designated program official responsible for monitoring technical and administrative performance of contracted operational support personnel.

Provides executive oversight of threat management, intelligence intake and triage operations, event security coordination, law enforcement information sharing, residential security monitoring, travel monitoring, and protective operations support activities.

Oversees coordination among federal, state, and local partner agencies, as well as military, intelligence community, and Congressional stakeholders to ensure timely information sharing and effective operational support.

Provides executive oversight for significant incidents, emergency response activities, continuity of operations programs, and crisis management efforts affecting the agency’s protective mission.

Serves as a member of emergency response and continuity planning teams responsible for maintaining operational readiness during emergencies, natural disasters, civil disturbances, security incidents, and other disruptive events.
In order to qualify, you must meet the education and/or experience requirements described below. For the CP-12 you must have at least 52 weeks of specialized experience equivalent to the CP-11/GS-13 level that is in or directly related to the line of work of the position to be filled.

Specialized experience consists of: 1) contributing to oversight and strategic direction for a 24-hour operational environment responsible for law enforcement or protective intelligence; 2) leading and directing complex research, intelligence analysis, and evaluation activities related to investigative operations to support operational strategy and organizational decision-making; 3) demonstrated experience formulating information source search strategies and evaluating data to identify patterns and relationships across criminal, public records or other sources; and 4) compile complex investigative information from a variety of sources in order to communicate and/or present investigative information orally and in writing to a variety of audiences.

Raisin is the world’s leading platform for savings and investment products. Founded in 2012, the FinTech connects consumers with banks in the EU, the UK and the US. This gives consumers better interest rates and banks a diversified form of refinancing . Our vision is to offer savings and investments without barriers and thus open up the global 160 trillion euro market.
Raisin currently employs more than 800 people from over 75 countries worldwide. Today, the platform holds over 80 billion euros in assets from more than one million investors which have accrued over 5 billion euros in returns.
Team
The Custody & Principal Broking team serves as the backbone of Raisin Bank’s Digital Wealth Management (DWM) division, providing the secure, scalable foundation essential for retail investing.

We manage the complex infrastructure, from securities trading mechanics to outsourcing oversight that ensures operational resilience and regulatory compliance.

As our retail customer base grows, we are focused on continuous process optimization and high-volume scalability, ensuring our platforms remain reliable, secure, and fully compliant with BaFin standards. We are currently seeking a Senior Operations Manager to join this mission.

Strategic Process Optimization: You will drive the evolution of operational workflows to ensure they are scalable and resilient, directly supporting high-volume retail growth.
Operational Controls & Oversight: You will define and execute the control framework for daily securities processing, ensuring rigorous validation of all outsourced clearing and settlement activities.
Regulatory Compliance: You will partner with Compliance, Legal, and Risk teams to navigate the regulatory landscape and maintain strict adherence to German financial regulations (including KWG, WpHG, and MaRisk).
Operational Resilience: You will proactively investigate, moderate, and resolve complex securities discrepancies and trade breaks in close collaboration with cross-functional internal and external stakeholders.
Due Diligence & Auditing: You will actively support due diligence activities and comprehensive audits for both current and prospective outsourcing partners.
Strategic Project Contribution: You will provide subject matter expertise for internal and external strategic initiatives, including product launches, platform upgrades, and system migrations.
Your Profile
Education: Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Finance, Economics, Business Administration, or a completed banking apprenticeship (Bankkaufmann/-frau) with relevant further qualifications.
Experience: 7+ years of operations experience within a custodian bank (Depotbank), clearing firm, or retail broker in the German/European market.
Private Customer Expertise: Direct experience with mass-affluent and high-volume retail accounts, managing the complexities of fractional shares, and savings plans (Sparpläne).
Technical & Market Knowledge: Deep understanding of Clearstream Banking Frankfurt (CBF), T2S, and European post-trade infrastructure.
Risk & Controls: Proven background in establishing and executing internal controls, particularly within the context of MaRisk and outsourced operations.
Language Skills: Business fluency in both German and English is required.

About Substrate
Substrate is the critical infrastructure layer between AI and biology. AI for biology has a data problem, not a compute problem: biological foundation models can predict but cannot experiment, and the large-scale, high-quality data they need does not exist. We are building the lab that generates it, with quality and provenance built in. We are not a CRO and we are not a cloud lab.
The company was founded by Mostafa ElSayed, co-founder and CEO; Oli Hoy, who leads the lab buildout and operations; Alexey Morgunov, who leads science and intelligence software; and Anna Huyghues-Despointes, who leads partnerships and go-to-market.

You will run the day-to-day operations of our lab in London, and be the person the scientists come to when something is missing, broken, late or lost. The day-one work is what you would expect: consumables and stock, goods in and cold chain, equipment servicing and calibration, suppliers and purchasing, waste streams and safety records.
Three parts go beyond a standard lab operations job. The first is provenance. Every experiment we sell carries a record of what went into it, down to the lot of the consumable used and the conditions material was held in. If a lot number is not captured, the data point is worth less, and that record runs through you.
The second is that the systems are not written yet. Inventory, goods in, asset registers and ordering exist in no form that will survive the next year. You define what the lab has to capture and work with the science and software teams to make sure it does.
The third is that sample handling and stock control here get automated, and you help specify the system that does it. Every sample, plate, reagent and consumable lot carries a barcode, scanned at each point it is handled, so the record is created by the work rather than reconstructed afterwards.

The same scan draws stock down, which turns reordering from a weekly count into something the system flags before anyone is short. Our software team is building that layer now and the requirements have to come from the lab floor: what gets a barcode, where the scan points sit, and what happens when a label will not read.

Some find that energising; some find it outside their lane. Worth knowing which one you are.
Your first 90 days
First 30 days
Take ownership of goods in: every delivery received, booked in, stored correctly and recorded.
Map how material moves through the lab and build the first accurate picture of what we hold. That map is the input to a fully barcoded scheme and system.
Days 30 to 60
Put a working inventory and reorder system in place, with minimum levels set from real consumption rather than guesses, and own the purchasing loop.
Agree the barcode and labelling scheme with the software team, and get equipment records in one place.
Days 60 to 90
Run the lab as a routine that does not depend on being asked, with the barcoded system live across one workflow, goods-in to bench to stock draw-down, feeding our provenance record.

You have run the physical side of a lab where being out of stock stops the work: biotech, pharma, a university or institute lab, or a manufacturing or diagnostics operation built around one.

Lab consumables and the rhythm of a working lab are already familiar to you, you have handled real volume and real inventory, and you know the difference between a system that works on paper and one that works at eight on a Monday morning.

We are not asking for a particular speciality, but you should arrive able to run the lab rather than learn what one needs.

Two or more years running a lab or comparable physical operation, hands-on and accountable for the result.
Practical stock control: goods in, inventory records, reorder points, stock counts that reconcile.
Buying from suppliers: raising orders, comparing quotes, managing lead times.
Hands-on with a barcoded or scanned stock system, including what goes wrong when people skip the scan.
Lab environment experience: cold storage, hazardous waste, containment, controlled materials.

Health and safety training such as IOSH.
Developed or co-developed a barcode system for autonomous workflows in labs, including working with software development teams to implement it.
How we work and who you will work with
This role is on site five days a week at 20 Triton Street in London, because the lab is a physical place and the work is in it. The wider founding team is distributed across London, New York and Europe.

You will report to Simon Varzandeh, a member of our scientific staff working on protein characterisation and one of the lab's heaviest users, and work alongside the protein science and functional genomics teams, the engineers building the tracking and stock system with you, and operations on facilities, health and safety and purchasing.

You will be the first person here whose whole job is focused on the lab floor.
We work in the open and each person owns their area. UK benefits are 30 days of annual leave plus public holidays, a pension with a 10% employer contribution, and top-tier Bupa private health cover.
